question: Two teams, one seed, no games left against each other - what decides it?

headline.text: Golden State Valkyries and Indiana Fever have no meetings left. Golden State closes 3 of 10 at home; Indiana closes 3 of 8.

body: Golden State Valkyries and Indiana Fever are fighting for the second seed - and they will never see each other again. Zero head-to-head games remain. From here, the race is decided entirely by proxy: by geography, by rest, and by how each team survives Minnesota.

The proxies are not neutral. Golden State closes with three of ten at home. Indiana closes three of eight at home. Two teams separated by 2.7 of a win in our projections, separated by several points of schedule context.

Then there is the Minnesota gauntlet: four of the highest-leverage remaining games in the league are these two teams against the Lynx - August 19 and August 24 for Golden State, September 22 and September 24 for Indiana. Split them and the schedule edge probably decides it. Sweep or get swept, and the proxies stop mattering.
Watch the rest columns, not the rivalry - there isn't one left to watch.
